{{short description|American educational psychologist}}
'''Joan B. Garfield''' is an American [[educational psychology|educational psychologist]] specializing in [[statistics education]]. She is retired from the [[University of Minnesota]] as a professor emeritus of educational psychology.

==Education==
Garfield entered the [[University of Wisconsin]] intending to study [[anthropology]],{{r|ros}} but graduated in 1972 with a bachelor's degree in education and a minor in mathematics.{{r|cv}} She became a middle school mathematics teacher but, realizing she needed more preparation as a teacher, returned to graduate school. She chose the [[University of Minnesota]] hoping to work with Donovan Johnson, whose works she had read, but he had retired and she instead worked with his student Robert Jackson.{{r|ros}} She earned a master's degree in mathematics education from the University of Minnesota in 1978,{{r|cv}} and while working on it was encouraged by statistician Raymond O. Collier Jr. to continue for doctoral studies.{{r|ros}} She completed her Ph.D. in educational psychology from the University of Minnesota in 1981.{{r|cv}}

==Career==
Garfield began teaching at University of Minnesota faculty in 1979 as a summer mathematics instructor,{{r|cv}} as a way of supplementing her income as a graduate student,{{r|ros}} and remained at the university for the rest of her career, becoming a full professor in 2002.{{r|cv}}

She chaired the [[American Statistical Association]] Section on Statistics Education in 2003, and in the same year was president of the [[American Educational Research Association]] Special Interest Group for Educational Statisticians.{{r|cv}}

==Books==
Garfield is the editor of several books in statistics education{{r|cv}} and the author, with Dani Ben Zvi, of ''Developing Students’ Statistical Reasoning: Connecting Research and Teaching Practice'' (Springer, 2008).{{r|dssr}}

==Recognition==
In 2001 Garfield was recognized as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fi}} She has been an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] since 2002. In 2005 the American Statistical Association gave her their [[American Statistical Association Founders Award|Founder's Award]] for distinguished service to the association. The Consortium for the Advancement of Undergraduate Statistics Education gave her their lifetime achievement award in 2007.{{r|cv}}
